studies.Population: Human study population described in the cited article
studies.Ethnicity Basis: NA: no field-specific ethnicity evidence was available
studies.Reference: Diet and bladder cancer: a case-control study.
studies.Authors: Radosavljević V, Janković S, Marinković J, Dokić M
studies.Timing: Dietary intake assessed in newly diagnosed cases
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Dietary information was obtained by using a food frequency questionnaire.

cases.excerpt: This study included 130 newly diagnosed bladder cancer patients and the same number of controls matched by sex, age (%+/-%2 years) and type of residence (rural or urban).

effect_size.excerpt: According to this analysis, risk factors for bladder cancer appeared to be consumption of liver (OR=6.60, 95%CI=1.89-23.03), eggs (OR=3.12, 95%CI=1.10-8.80), pork (OR=2.99, 95%CI=1.16-7.72), and pickled vegetable (OR=3.25, 95%CI=1.36-7.71).

confidence_interval.excerpt: According to this analysis, risk factors for bladder cancer appeared to be consumption of liver (OR=6.60, 95%CI=1.89-23.03), eggs (OR=3.12, 95%CI=1.10-8.80), pork (OR=2.99, 95%CI=1.16-7.72), and pickled vegetable (OR=3.25, 95%CI=1.36-7.71).

comparison.excerpt: The odds ratios (ORs) were computed for each tertile, with the lowest tertile defined as the referent category.

design.excerpt: the hospital-based case-control study was carried out

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Dietary information was obtained by using a food frequency questionnaire.
